\begin{abstract}
Skateboard Physics (benchmark-skateboard) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.2.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 72 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2 on the public task split generated with seed 20261015. The review record shows 3 fix rounds, 4 defect classes with public locators, and 4 merged feature pull requests of which 2 were approved. The best trivial policy scored 0.0000 at both versions. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422365, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-skateboard/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
Can a model keep a kickflip, a heelflip, and gravity straight at the
same time? \textbf{benchmark-skateboard} measures signed 3D trick
rotations, projectile-motion arithmetic, wheels-down orientation, and
whether a trick can finish before landing.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-skateboard/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-skateboard:README.md\#L7}}.}

Its index entry states the measured construct as: ``Signed 3D rotation understanding, projectile-motion arithmetic, landing orientation, and whether a skateboard trick fits its airtime.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-skateboard.whatItMeasures}).

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-skateboard/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
The grader reads model text, strips one surrounding Markdown code
fence when present, parses the last balanced JSON object in the text,
and awards deterministic partial credit. It does not call a model.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-skateboard/blob/v0.2.0/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-skateboard:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Strict JSON shape; exact signed rotations in turns; 5\% relative tolerance for airtime and peak height; landing and feasibility booleans scored only when both physics values are within tolerance.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-skateboard.grader}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
over the public task split generated with seed \pkgPublicSeed{}, on version \pkgVersion{}:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
The preregistered check ran \pkgTrivialPolicies{} generic trivial policies against this package at versions
\pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{}. The best trivial score was \pkgTrivialOld{} at \pkgTrivialVerOld{}
and \pkgTrivialNew{} at \pkgTrivialVerNew{}, won by \texttt{\pkgTrivialPolicy{}} (\texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv}).
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-skateboard/README.md#L119
\begin{quote}
The flight model ignores drag, deck inertia, foot contact, body
rotation, and unequal landing height.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-skateboard/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#L119}{\texttt{benchmark-skateboard:README.md\#L119}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
